note: Macro events and crises that the letters themselves discuss. event_years = when it happened; letter_years = letters that discuss it beyond a passing mention (judged by reading; a letter for year Y is written early in Y+1). Annotators tag a passage with an event id when the passage is ABOUT that event, using the event's description (Buffett rarely uses the common names). Retrospective mentions in later letters are found through the passage tags, not through letter_years. After wave 1, M1 recomputes per-event tagged-passage counts and letter years from the event tags and stores them in knowledge_v1. The query router maps user wording to event ids through aliases and event_years.

provenance.built: 2026-10-19 by plan-fix group 1 (finding g1-1, with g1-7 and g1-8)
provenance.method: Corpus only (input/chunks_v3_paragraph.jsonl, 5,831 passages). Candidate passages were found by keyword search and each candidate was read; an event is kept when at least 5 passages discuss it, judged by reading, not by keyword counts. supporting_passages lists every passage judged to discuss the event (including later look-backs); supporting_count is its length.
provenance.alias_rule: Every alias occurs verbatim (case-insensitive, after quote/whitespace normalisation) in at least one of the event's supporting passages; alias_corpus_counts gives the number of corpus passages containing it. No alias is taken from user, dev-set or test-set wording.
provenance.test_set_access: None. No finance_v1*, split, heldout or sealed file was opened. The builder read the plan-review findings, which quote some dev-question wording; the alias rule keeps such wording out unless the letters themselves use it.

bear_market_1973_74.description: The 1973-74 stock-market collapse and the 1974-75 insurance underwriting crisis: bargain prices, Berkshire's own losses and share-price fall then, and later letters looking back at that period.

high_inflation_late70s_early80s.description: The high inflation of the late 1970s and early 1980s and what it did to business returns, insurance costs, bonds and investors (the 'inflation tax'); not general mentions of inflation in other years (those get theme inflation only).

crash_1987.description: The October 1987 market crash (Buffett: 'the break in October', Mr. Market's 'sudden, massive seizure'), portfolio insurance and the market turmoil around it, and later look-backs at it.

banking_real_estate_1990.description: The 1989-91 bank and savings-and-loan troubles, the fear of a California real-estate collapse (Wells Fargo bought amid the flight from bank stocks) and the 1990-91 recession's effect on Berkshire businesses.

salomon_1991.description: The 1991 Salomon scandal: Buffett as interim chairman, the government matters, the rescue of the firm and his look-back on it; not passages that only list the Salomon preferred as a holding.

hurricane_andrew_1992.description: Hurricane Andrew (1992): the largest insured loss up to then, its effect on the industry and on Berkshire's super-cat business, and later comparisons with it.

dotcom_bubble.description: The late-1990s internet/tech stock bubble Buffett calls 'The Great Bubble', speculation in bubble companies, its end in 2000 and its aftermath for valuations and corporate behaviour.

ltcm_1998.description: The 1998 near-collapse of the hedge fund Long-Term Capital Management and the Fed-organised rescue, discussed in the 2002 letter as an example of derivatives linkage risk.
ltcm_1998.kept_below_threshold: kept by verdict g1-1 (confirmed_with_change keeps ltcm_1998); only 2 passages discuss it

accounting_scandals_2002.description: The 2001-2002 corporate accounting scandals (Enron and others), pro-forma earnings games, the 'anything-goes' reporting era and the governance and audit-committee reforms that followed.

sept11_2001.description: The September 11, 2001 attacks: the insurance industry's largest loss, General Re's underwriting failure on terrorism risk, effects on Berkshire businesses (FlightSafety, NetJets, XTRA, FINOVA) and terrorism coverage written afterwards.

katrina_2005.description: Hurricane Katrina and the other 2005 hurricanes: record insured losses for Berkshire and the industry, super-cat pricing and the question of changed hurricane frequency, and later comparisons with Katrina.

financial_crisis_2008.description: The 2007-09 housing bust, credit crisis and financial panic and the recession that followed: mortgage and housing passages, Fannie/Freddie, Berkshire's investments during the panic, its businesses in the recession, and later look-backs.

tax_act_2017.description: The December 2017 U.S. tax law that cut the corporate rate to 21%: the $29 billion gain it delivered to Berkshire's net worth in 2017 and its effect on 2018 after-tax earnings and intrinsic value.
